summary: Gives IANA direction for creating and managing the IANA IPv4 Special Purpose Address Registry, which records reserved address blocks. It is informational and was replaced by RFC 6890.

eli5.summary: Someone needs to keep the list of special-purpose addresses up to date. This document tells the keeper of the list how to set it up. It was replaced by RFC 6890.

questions: what is the iana ipv4 special purpose address registry
who maintains the list of reserved ipv4 blocks
how does iana designate special purpose addresses
subtitle: Creating a registry for special-purpose IPv4 address blocks reserved by IANA.

tldr.problem: Various IPv4 address blocks are reserved for specialized uses, but there was no central, authoritative registry recording what they are, why they are reserved, and what they are used for.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC directs IANA to create and maintain the IANA IPv4 Special Purpose Address Registry, documenting all address blocks designated for protocol assignments, testing, or other special purposes.
tldr.outcome: The registry provides a trusted reference for special-purpose IPv4 addresses and helps the Internet community understand which addresses are reserved and for what purposes. RFC 6890 later updated this work.

today: RFC 5736 is an Informational RFC that directed IANA to establish the registry. It was later superseded by RFC 6890, which consolidated and updated the documentation of special-use IPv4 addresses. The registry itself remains an active and important reference for special-purpose address allocation.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: The IANA IPv4 Special Purpose Address Registry is a directory that records IPv4 address blocks reserved by the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) for specific technical purposes. These reserved address blocks serve roles like protocol testing, experimental use, or providing special-purpose services. This RFC directs IANA to create and manage this registry in compliance with existing procedures.
sections.eli5: Just like a library catalog keeps track of where all the books are, this registry keeps a list of special IPv4 addresses and what they are used for.

sections.title: The 192.0.0.0/24 Block
sections.content: RFC 5735 previously assigned 192.0.0.0/24 to IANA for IETF protocol assignments. This 256-address block is reserved specifically for allocating addresses to support Internet standards work. The registry will document how this block is used and track any future allocations of address space to IANA for special purposes.
sections.eli5: There is a special set of 256 addresses set aside for the people building Internet standards to use for testing and new protocols.

sections.title: What the Registry Records
sections.content: For each address block designated by IANA, the registry records: the address prefix itself, the RFC that requested the designation, the date the designation was made, any expiration date for the use, the purpose of the designation (such as unicast experiment or protocol service), contact details for experimental allocations, and the intended routing scope (whether the address is meant to stay local or route globally). New allocations from the special-purpose pool require approval from an IETF Review process.
sections.eli5: For each reserved address, the registry writes down what it is, why it is reserved, when it was reserved, and where it can be used.

sections.title: Security and Trust
sections.content: A trustworthy registry of special-purpose addresses helps secure Internet routing. To authenticate control of an address block, operators must verify that it belongs to an existing allocated range and is recorded in the IANA registries. This registry serves as an authoritative source for validating address ownership and preventing misuse. Future work should add digital signatures and certificates to let applications verify that registry contents are current and officially published by IANA.
sections.eli5: Knowing which addresses are official helps prevent someone from using an address they should not be using.
